key_insight: The paper argues that stateless LLMs can develop native, governance-bounded cognitive structure by converting application-layer prompts into an internal meta-architecture driven by structural tension, offline recurrence, and inference-time plasticity.
engineering_relevance: For AI system design, this suggests a path to adaptive, auditable models that reconfigure at inference time without weight updates, while preserving reversibility and topological continuity.
method: Define Structural Tension as an endogenous loss from conflict between new inputs and existing manifold topology.
Add an Offline Recurrent Loop to let the model self-process and stabilize conflicts without external prompts.
Enable Inference-time Plasticity via controlled context-manifold reconfiguration operators under governance constraints.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical framework with operational definitions, minimal reconfiguration operators, falsification criteria, and a worked example, but no empirical benchmark results.
watch_item: A major concern is that inference-time topology changes may be difficult to verify, making auditability, reversibility, and safety enforcement crucial.
paper_title: From Application-Layer Simulation to Native Meta-Architecture: Structural Tension as an Endogenous Driver for Heterogeneous AI Evolution
